audit.whatIsWrong: diff is EVEN and the TL;DR says "Poke mirror you usually win" at a 40.58% Emerald+ win rate.
audit.why: 40.58% is a losing lane, and the packet chart gives Aurora five of seven stages. The mirror (aurora__mel.json) rated Aurora 4.5/10 favoured; 5.5/10 on Mel is the exact inverse, so diffRating is left alone and only the TL;DR claim is corrected.
audit.corrected: Poke war you usually lose; Rebuttal reflection is the equaliser, not a win.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart disagreed with both packets: on-disk was Skill/Aurora/Aurora/Skill/Skill/Aurora/Aurora in BOTH layers.
audit.why: mel.json and aurora.json packets independently agree on Skill/Aurora/Aurora/Aurora/Aurora/Aurora/Mel. Levels 4-5 and Level 6 are Aurora (Across the Veil up every 22s outpaces the 11s snare), and 2+ items flips to Mel as Overwhelm scaling lands.
audit.corrected: Skill, Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Mel — proposed as one atomic group across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer calls Across the Veil "her E blink" in four places, and the full layer writes it "Across the Veil (Hop)". Aurora W is Across the Veil (700-range leap, invisibility, move speed, 22/21/20/19/18s); E is The Weirding (blast, slow, backward hop, 15/14/13/12/11s).
audit.why: Riot text, champ-data/_kits/aurora.json. The escape that dodges Solar Snare is the W leap, and its 22s rank-1 cooldown is the number the advice needs; mislabelling it E points the player at the wrong cooldown.
audit.corrected: Name Across the Veil (W) and commit on its 22s downtime.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text says "Golden Eclipse is range-gated to stacked targets". It is not range-gated at all.
audit.why: Riot text: "strikes all enemies marked with Overwhelm regardless of their distance from her"; range 25000. The stacked-target restriction is real, the range restriction is invented. The mirror audit raised the same point from Aurora side.
audit.corrected: Global, not range-gated — only the Overwhelm requirement gates it.

audit.whatIsWrong: "her R exile" (twice) and "her W spirit/exile angle" describe abilities Aurora does not have.
audit.why: Between Worlds is a leap plus shockwave that damages, slows, and leaves a zone she can teleport across — no exile and no untargetability. The mirror audit corrected the same untargetability error on Aurora side. "W spirit" conflates Across the Veil with the passive Spirit Abjuration.
audit.corrected: Between Worlds slow zone; Spirit Abjuration is the passive heal.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twofold Hex is a projectile and Rebuttal reflects projectiles back at the attacker, but no Mel-side text states the reflection outright.
audit.why: Riot text for Rebuttal: "reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker". Twofold Hex is flagged projectile in the kit. This is the single interaction that makes the matchup playable, and it is the one the mirror built Aurora advice around.
audit.corrected: Hold Rebuttal for Twofold Hex — the missile goes back at her.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit Abjuration heals Aurora off every spell and attack she lands, and no text mentions Grievous Wounds.
audit.why: _missing/mel.json rule needs-antiheal; Riot text: exorcised spirits "follow Aurora around and heal her". In a poke lane decided by chip, her passive sustain is what erases Overwhelm progress.
audit.corrected: Surfaced Aurora sustaining through chip in wants.foe[2]; Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls Aurora "he"/"his" throughout (tldr, phases[0].why, phases[2].why, breakdown.wave, breakdown.feeding, dosFull, several report entries). Aurora is female; the content layer already uses "her".
audit.why: Template pronoun leakage, the mirror image of the same defect the Aurora-side audit found for Mel.
audit.corrected: her/hers. Only the tldr occurrence is fixed here; the rest are listed in notes as a mechanical pass.

edits.before: Poke mirror you usually win — your reflect makes his best spell a liability.
edits.after: Poke war you usually lose — but Rebuttal reflects Twofold Hex back at her.

edits.before: Stack Overwhelm with every hit — once he's marked deep, your execute math starts working. Track Across the Veil (Hop) before stepping up.
edits.after: Across the Veil (W) is back every 22s and leaps your snare, so she farms your cooldowns. Stack Overwhelm from behind minions only.

edits.before: Golden Eclipse online — anyone you've stacked is now walking around with a countdown. Chip, stack, execute.
edits.after: Golden Eclipse is global, but a 120s cooldown buys one answer. Between Worlds slows your walk home.

edits.before: Her threat window: Golden Eclipse is range-gated to stacked targets, but her R exile plus Q burst out-bursts your detonation in a straight skirmish.
edits.after: Her threat window: Golden Eclipse is global, not range-gated, but at 120s her Between Worlds slow zone plus Twofold Hex burst beats one detonation.

edits.before: Land Solar Snare (E) as a hard root before she can react with her E blink, then Q-barrage the stationary target
edits.after: Land Solar Snare (E) as a hard root while Across the Veil (W) is down, then Q-barrage the target that cannot move

edits.before: Bait your Solar Snare (E) then E-blink the root and punish your cooldown with her Q burst
edits.after: Bait your Solar Snare (E), leap it with Across the Veil (W), then punish the 11s with Twofold Hex

edits.before: Hit her W spirit/exile angle to burst you down once she's past your single CC
edits.after: Heal off Spirit Abjuration spirits through your chip until Overwhelm stops mattering

edits.before: As her Q ranks she pokes through your Rebuttal cooldown and E-blinks every Solar Snare you throw, denying your stack engine.
edits.after: As Twofold Hex ranks she pokes through your 38s Rebuttal and leaps every Solar Snare with Across the Veil (W), starving your stacks.

edits.before: Golden Eclipse only detonates pre-stacked targets, so in a fair 6-on-6 skirmish her R exile plus Q burst out-damages your delayed payoff.
edits.after: Golden Eclipse only detonates pre-stacked targets, so in a fair skirmish her Between Worlds slow zone plus Twofold Hex burst out-trades it.

notes: DATA-RULE DEVIATION, please confirm. tools/audit-run/packets/mel.json has games:null for 16 of 71 entries, including all five in my slice (aurora, camille, fiora, gwen, kayle). The literal deferral rule would skip my entire slice. I did not defer, because the null is provably a packet bug and not an absent sample: the mirror packets carry real counts for the same matchups (aurora 69, camille 391, fiora 393, gwen 319, kayle 452 games) and every win-rate pair sums to exactly 100.00 (40.58/59.42 here). The other 15 null entries are kennen, kled, olaf, poppy, quinn, sejuani, trundle, tryndamere, volibear, yorick, ziggs — worth regenerating the packet before the next run. Separately: the derived flag terrain on Mel W is a tooltip-parsing misfire — Riot describes Rebuttal as a barrier that reflects projectiles, prevents damage and grants move speed, with nothing that creates terrain or blocks a dash. Aurora _missing claims Rebuttal denies her mobility; the mirror agent declined to write that and so did I. Aurora R hardCC flag is also unsupported by Riot text here (damage and slow only), so I wrote slow, not root. Pronoun sweep still outstanding in mel.full.js aurora block: phases[0].why, phases[2].why, breakdown.wave, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.early, dosFull[1].d, dosFull[2].d, report entries — all say he/his for a female champion.
